osaka_ramen_goku_honten.notes: [Ramen · light tonkotsu and egg-topped char-rice by Tennoji] A nine-seat, dimly lit counter about five minutes from Tennoji, known for its char-rice: fried rice under a fluffy omelet, seasoned lightly on purpose so you finish it with the garlic or wasabi sauces on the table. The tonkotsu comes white, black (with black garlic oil) or red, and one diner found it lighter and less salty than expected, closer to Mokkosu than Hakata; it comes with about five slices of chashu and wood ear mushroom. Extra back fat is free, and so are pickled ginger, spicy takana, grated garlic, fried onion and mayonnaise. The Manpuku set pairs a bowl with a small char-rice. A chashu chuka soba (¥1,300) on thick noodles is the other option. Free half-size kaedama until 15:00 on weekdays. Buy tickets at the machine outside; cash or PayPay only.

chef_bio.background: Tonkotsu ramen shop, main store (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: "A shop that seriously makes pork bone soup" (shop phrase quoted in an October 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Tonkotsu ramen in three styles; char-rice.

anecdotes.text: "The ramen is tonkotsu and you can choose from white, black, or red. I opted for the black with black garlic oil… The char rice, which is fried rice topped with an omelet, was incredibly tasty. The omelet was fluffy…" — September 2026, Manpuku set.
"The flavor was lighter and less salty than I expected, resembling more of a Mokkosu style than Hakata. I ordered extra fat, but it wasn't overwhelming…" — September 2026.

osaka_chuka_soba_tsuji_tenmabashi.notes: [Ramen · punchy chili-and-garlic chuka soba by Tenmabashi] An eleven-seat shop a minute from Tenmabashi, open since 2023 and now busy thanks to social media: check in on the touch panel out front and expect a wait (about 25 minutes to get in, one August lunch). The chuka soba is shoyu loaded with chili and fresh garlic; one diner calls this kind of punch rare in Kansai, where Mongolian Tanmen Nakamoto has no shops, while another found it a fairly standard shoyu with chili. The beef horumon chuka soba brings more chili and garlic, and one diner found the sour and spicy djanmen (¥1,800) rich to the last bite. Limited bowls rotate: Bachiro (¥1,100 with extra sprouts) on borrowed noodles, and a chilled tantan mazesoba in summer. Add a meat-taku rice bowl (¥550). Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.specialty: Spicy chuka soba with chili and garlic; limited bowls.

anecdotes.text: "The Chuka Soba here is known for its spiciness, featuring chili peppers as a highlight. I ordered the spicy Chuka Soba with beef offal in a large size." — August 2026; about 25 minutes in line to get inside.
"I added some garlic from the table and got ready to dig in. This chuka soba seemed like it was made just for someone like me, who loves garlic and chili." — October 2026, beef horumon chuka soba.

Buy tickets at the machine; state noodle firmness, flavor strength and oil when handing it over. Cards, IC cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_iekei_semba_ya_tsuruhashi.notes: [Ramen · lighter iekei with smoked chashu by Tsuruhashi] An eight-seat counter about ten minutes from Tsuruhashi, open since May 2025, with lines on weekends. The broth of pork bones and chicken carcasses is creamy and rich but easy to drink, with a mild soy tare and chicken oil, over chewy medium-thick short noodles from Inoue Seimen; order firmness, flavor and oil to taste. Smoked, oven-roasted thigh chashu (firm and meaty) and shredded chashu sit with komatsuna and nori. The jō ramen (¥1,000) adds chashu, nori and half an egg. Rice is free at lunch; top it with the pickled cucumber and furikake, and finish with doubanjiang from the table. One diner calls it possibly the best iekei in Osaka; another found the broth thinner and the chashu dry on a later visit. Staff see you off at the door.

chef_bio.specialty: Iekei ramen with smoked thigh chashu.

anecdotes.text: "The broth, made from simmered pork bones and chicken carcasses, has a rich umami flavor. It strikes a nice balance with a mild soy sauce taste, making it easy to drink… The noodles are medium-thick, short noodles from Inoue Seimen…" — September 2026, jō ramen ¥1,000.

"The noodles were thick and had a strong texture, giving a firm impression with less chewiness. The chashu was moist and tender, with a perfect contrast of smoky flavor and meaty goodness." — October 2026, firm noodles and extra oil.

osaka_maren_higobashi.notes: [Ramen · tidy mazesoba with a rice finish at Higobashi] An eleven-seat shop right by Higobashi exit 9, open since April 2023 and part of MAREN, the mazesoba shop with a branch in Shinsaibashi. The shoyu mazesoba (¥980) coats thick, chewy noodles in a sauce that's rich but not heavy and arrives neatly arranged; add niboshi vinegar halfway, then mix the small scoop of rice into what's left. The chicken shio mazesoba gets its lift from shiso, and there's a chicken shoyu chashu version. The chicken paitan ramen is less loved: one diner saw it made from powders blended into a clear liquid on an IH burner. Order on the touch panel. Lines build after 12:00, so go early or late. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Mazesoba shop; sister shop of MAREN Shinsaibashi (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The thick noodles are coated in a flavorful sauce that's delicious! It's rich but not too heavy… I added some niboshi vinegar for a flavor change, which made it even smoother!" — October 2026, shoyu mazesoba.
"To finish off, you can mix in a small plate of rice, which is so tasty that I can't help but finish it all…" — September 2026, shoyu mazesoba ¥980.

osaka_ramen_three_hanare_higobashi.notes: [Ramen · clam-broth ramen and a ¥650 breakfast bowl at Higobashi] A stylish ten-seat counter three minutes from Higobashi, open since October 2025 and sharing its name with Ramen ThreE nearby. The house bowl is a light broth of clam, scallop and dried seafood, with clam out front, over straight, medium-thin low-hydration noodles, topped with two kinds of chicken chashu and rare pork loin; sansho from the table lifts the aroma. There's also a clam and Kyoto bonito chuka soba, a creamy clam-and-pork shio and a rich tonkotsu shoyu. On weekdays it opens at 7:00 for morning ramen (¥650) with free egg-over-rice or natto rice. One diner found the morning bowls a bit salty. Register on LINE and the fourth bowl is free. Cards and QR accepted.

anecdotes.text: "The soup was a blend of clam, scallop, and dried seafood, with the clam flavor being slightly dominant. It was a light broth… The noodles were straight, medium-thin, and had a low water content, giving them a nice bite." — October 2026, clam tare ramen (shoyu).
"With the morning ramen, you can enjoy free egg over rice or natto rice. Both the Shoyu Ramen and the clam broth ramen are priced the same at JPY 650." — October 2026.

osaka_okamoto_shoten_hanare_tenmabashi.notes: [Ramen · chicken stewed ramen and lunch sets, izakaya by night, by Tenmabashi] A fifteen-seat basement counter on Tanimachi-suji, five minutes from Tenmabashi, serving ramen at lunch and turning into an all-you-can-eat-and-drink izakaya in the evening; by name and one diner's account, it is a branch of Okamoto Shoten near Kitahama. The chicken stewed ramen (¥950, with chashu and egg) looks rich and frothy but drinks smooth, with chicken sweetness. The menu is long: sets pair a bowl with a mini rice bowl, chicken curry or kara-age, and there's seafood shoyu with rare chashu, chicken paitan tsukemen and a spicy seafood ramen that one diner found heavy and short on seafood. Another found the ramen average but good value. From 13:30 a mini rice bowl is free. Cash or PayPay; smoking allowed.

anecdotes.text: "The chicken simmered ramen looked quite rich with its frothy appearance, but surprisingly, it wasn't too heavy. The broth was smooth, with a delightful balance of chicken umami and sweetness." — September 2026, set F ¥1,000.

osaka_menya_shin_yodoyabashi.notes: [Ramen · seafood-and-chicken paitan in the Yodoyabashi basement] An eight-seat, calm, Japanese-style counter in the basement of the Keihan Yodoyabashi Building, reachable underground from Yodoyabashi and Kitahama, open since 2023 as a new concept from Yawaragi, an izakaya in Shinsaibashi. The ramen (¥850) is a double soup of seafood and chicken paitan, slightly thick, rich but easy to drink, with the seafood coming through as you slurp the thin, firm, low-hydration Menya Teigaku noodles. Tender pork-belly chashu comes in thick slices in the chashu ramen (¥1,000). Finish with Dive Rice: kimchi rice you drop into the last of the soup. Rice is half price at lunch. Pay as you order. Cards and QR accepted.

osaka_mendokoro_hack_kujo.notes: [Ramen · kombu-shellfish chuka soba and seasonal white soups, with wok fried rice, by Kujo] A clean counter by Kujo Station, open here since April 2025 after moving from Namba, where you can watch the fried rice tossed in the wok and the bowls carefully plated. The fried rice, fluffy with burnt soy and optional butter, draws its own fans (one diner warns it can taste a bit salty), and the set (¥1,580) pairs it with a bowl. Warm service. Buy a ticket at the entrance; cash only. Closed Thursdays.

A fried mehikari roll and milk pudding close it out. Two seatings nightly, weekend lunch, reserve by the day before; 5% service charge.

osaka_jidori_nabe_miura_higashishinsaiba.notes: [Chicken · mizutaki hot pot of jidori chicken in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, Japanese-style mizutaki specialist on the fifth floor of a bar building just off the arcade from Shinsaibashi, with a short counter, low kotatsu tables and three staff. The courses start with chicken plates (peperoncino, a tsukune hamburger, chicken prosciutto, and sashimi on the Sai course) before the hot pot, which staff cook for you. Gunma black chicken is tender in a rich but not heavy broth, with soft cabbage, grated yam and house yuzu-kosho. Finish with broth poured over rice, zosui or tea rice. One diner liked the pasta with lettuce enough to want seconds. Courses run from the small Hashi upward. Seen off at the elevator. Cards accepted; closed Sundays.

Unlike the usual soy-heavy Jiro bowl, the soup is a creamy, emulsified tonkotsu, slightly sweet and not too salty, so even extra back fat goes down easily. Noodles are medium-thick, flat and straight, smooth rather than chewy. Pick the noodle weight (150–300 g) and your garlic, vegetables and fat on the touch panel, so there's no call to learn; extra vegetables can water the soup down. There's also miso, soupless and tsukemen. Vinegar or fish powder from the table changes the flavor. Expect a line at opening; keep the narrow sidewalk clear. Cash only. Kept clean.

osaka_monja_mugi_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Monjayaki · Tsukishima-style monja cooked at your table, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A lively second-floor monjayaki spot near Shinsaibashi that cooks in the Tsukishima, Tokyo style, rare in Osaka, with staff doing the work on the hot plate in front of you. The batter has a rich dashi base. The classic is the Mugi Special; the mentaiko mochi cheese is the other standby, best with crispy edges and an egg yolk stirred in. Customize with chikuwa, corn and Baby Star, or try rotating monja such as Komtang or Shin Ramyeon. Tonpei-yaki, okonomiyaki and simple sides (avocado sashimi, diced cucumber) fill the gaps. osaka_rokumeikan_shinsaibashi.notes: [Kissa · a retro coffee house with European-style curry, Shinsaibashi] An old kissa tucked into an alley just off Shinsaibashi-suji, easy to walk past, with a nostalgic, unhurried interior, a big speaker by the counter and pretty cups. The draw besides the coffee is the Rokumeikan curry (¥1,200): a tangy, gently spicy European-style curry with whole potatoes, a soft-boiled egg and sausage, eaten with knife and fork. One diner found the potato cold in the middle, and coffee on top brings it past ¥1,800. Booth seats are mostly self-service. Tabelog lists 14:00–19:00, but late-2025 reviews describe it opening at night as a bar, so check. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Long-running kissa (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews); featured over two pages in a book on Osaka coffee houses (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The curry comes with chunks of potato, a soft-boiled egg, and sausage… As for the flavor, it has a strong acidity and a hint of spiciness." — September 2026, Rokumeikan curry ¥1,200.
"With its nostalgic atmosphere from a bygone era, the interior is incredibly calming." — December 2025.

osaka_takoyaki_oden_tomono_namba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: clam broth throughout; octopus; fish cakes.
osaka_takoyaki_oden_tomono_namba.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–05:00 (last order 04:00); open year-round (Tabelog). Appetizer charge ¥440 (Tabelog). Busy; seats refill fast (February 2026). Cards and PayPay accepted; no e-money (Tabelog).
osaka_takoyaki_oden_tomono_namba.notes: [Izakaya · clam-broth oden and fresh takoyaki until 5 am, Namba] A busy oden-and-takoyaki izakaya thirty seconds from Namba exit 32, open nightly from 18:00 to 5:00. The oden simmers in a clam broth, comes in small, shareable plates (staff will cut it for a group), and arrives with the plump broth clams themselves; the list runs to unusual picks like pea shoots and bean sprouts. The takoyaki is grilled only after you order, so it lands hot and gooey; try it with salt to taste the broth in the batter, or soaked in the clam broth. One diner rates it above a famous takoyaki shop. Easy solo, too. ¥440 appetizer charge.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 26 April 2019 (Tabelog); has a Shinsaibashi branch (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "All the oden is tasty, but the takoyaki is exceptional. The flavor of the broth is intense… When you eat it with salt, you can really taste it… [It is grilled] fresh after you order…" — July 2026.
"The oden menu was extensive, featuring unique items like pea shoots and bean sprouts that I don't usually see…" — September 2026.

osaka_tori_ryori_torisho_higashishinsaib.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 18:00–00:30 (last order 24:00); closed Mon; hours may change (Tabelog). Kamameshi takes about 40 minutes; order early (October 2025). Appetizer charge ¥500 (Tabelog). Cards and e-money accepted; smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_tori_ryori_torisho_higashishinsaib.notes: [Yakitori · chicken izakaya with double-cheese tsukune and kamameshi, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm second-floor chicken restaurant near Shinsaibashi, open since 2011, with a counter and a few tables. Start with the W cheese tsukune, which looks nothing like what you expect, and the skin, grilled crisp outside but still fluffy. Liver and heart are rich, and the chicken sashimi is fresh and clean. Order the kamameshi when you sit down; it takes about 40 minutes. The skewers come with a sweet tare; finish with egg over rice. Staff are friendly and have helped stage a surprise celebration with a cake. ¥500 appetizer charge. Smoking allowed. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.specialty: Yakitori; cheese tsukune; chicken sashimi; kamameshi.

anecdotes.text: "And the skin! At most places, the fat is rendered out, leaving the skin dry and crispy, but here it's both crispy and fluffy, which is surprising." — October 2025.

"The chicken sashimi was incredibly fresh, with a melt-in-your-mouth texture and no unpleasant odor… I heard that the kamameshi takes about 40 minutes to cook, so I ordered it right away." — October 2025.

osaka_tsukemen_rocky_tenmabashi.notes: [Tsukemen · seafood-tonkotsu tsukemen near Tenmabashi] A tsukemen shop a few minutes from Tenmabashi, open since 2022, that one diner calls the place for tsukemen in the area. The thick, chewy noodles come neatly laid out next to a rich seafood and pork-bone dip with chunks of chashu in it; the special (two big slices of chashu, nori and an egg) is the full version, and a spicy kara tsukemen is the alternative. Add the grilled, thick-cut chashu topping (¥350) and yuzu shichimi from the table, then ask for soup to dilute the last of the dip. Two diners found the dip went lukewarm quickly. Large is ¥100 more. Ticket machine; PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 11 February 2022 (Tabelog); has a sister restaurant (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The satisfying tsukemen paired with the seafood-based dipping sauce was absolutely delightful. Adding yuzu shichimi gave it a nice accent, making it even tastier." — September 2026, tsukemen ¥1,000, chashu ¥350, large ¥100.

"The flavor was a delightful seafood and pork bone broth… There was chashu in the soup, but the topping was grilled and cut a bit thicker, which made it delicious." — October 2026, large tsukemen with chashu.

osaka_yakimeshi_to_men_tenmabashi.notes: [Ramen · fried rice and light chuka soba by Tenmabashi] A small shop right by Tenmabashi Station, open since 2024, whose banner and name put the fried rice first. Buy a ticket downstairs (cash, no big notes), then climb a steep, narrow staircase to the seats. The usual order is the set (¥1,280–1,290): a light shoyu chuka soba on thin, straight noodles with a soba-like bite, rare chashu and thick menma, plus half a plate of fragrant, fluffy fried rice. Opinions split: several diners call the fried rice the reason to come, while others found both mild, and one saw the set cost ¥980 a week earlier. Water and dish return are self-service.

chef_bio.background: Fried rice and chuka soba shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles had a texture more similar to soba than ramen, and the broth was on the lighter side… The fried rice, on the other hand, was rich in flavor and to my liking." — August 2026, fried rice set.

osaka_chuka_restaurant_ajiichi_tsuruhash.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun 11:00–21:00; closed Wed and Sat; hours may change (Tabelog). Order verbally (May 2026). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR; smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_chuka_restaurant_ajiichi_tsuruhash.notes: [Chinese · a station-front local Chinese since 1985, Tsuruhashi] A long-running local Chinese restaurant a minute from Tsuruhashi Station, with a classic red counter downstairs and tables upstairs, open since 1985. The specialty is a sauce yakisoba in the style of Osaka's Imazato yakisoba (¥1,000): thick noodles in a rich sauce with pork, shrimp, squid, green pepper and a fried egg on top. Lunch sets are the other draw, such as set B (¥1,080) with standout sweet and sour pork, kara-age and a crab omelet. There's also crab fried rice (¥800), gyoza (¥370) and noodle soups. One diner found the kara-age batter tempura-like, another the portions small. Cards accepted; smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays and Saturdays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Yakisoba with roots in Imazato yakisoba (May 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "This local specialty, 'Imazato Yakisoba,' features pork, cabbage, onions, and custom thick noodles stir-fried in a rich sauce, topped with green peppers, large shrimp, small shrimp, a fried egg, shredded nori, and squid." — May 2026, special sauce yakisoba ¥1,000.
"I was impressed by the high level of the sweet and sour pork! The sauce was so rich that I felt it was the star of the set." — May 2026, set B ¥1,080.

osaka_kamigata_rainbow_momodani.notes: [Ramen · inventive six-seat ramen on homemade fettuccine noodles, Momodani] A six-seat shop with a storefront that doesn't look like a ramen shop, five minutes from Momodani, open since 2020. The menu has a steady core and a stream of playful limited bowls. The standout for several diners is the Shoyu Animal (¥1,600), a deep, sweet, umami-heavy animal broth; the iriko shoyu and shio (¥1,000 each) are simpler. The limited tsukemen use homemade flat, thick fettuccine-style noodles, such as a pear and Aka Buta DDX pork tsukemen, an unagi dashi version or a fig and octopus salt dip. Staff suggest trying the noodles first with just salt and lemon. Check Instagram for the current menu. Order on the tablet. Closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop with a rotating limited menu (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Homemade flat, thick fettuccine-style noodles; recommends tasting them with salt and lemon first (October 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The dipping sauce was a pork bone-based soy sauce with a slight tang… The noodles were homemade flat, thick fettuccine-style, with a nice chewy texture… Adding salt and wasabi to the noodles provided a great accent." — October 2026, Aka Buta DDX autumn pear tsukemen ¥1,600.
"I just love this soup too much!! The rich umami and sweetness from the animal-based broth are incredible!" — October 2026, Shoyu Animal ¥1,600.

Summer brings chilled bowls. Weekday specials before 19:00 include a ¥800 shoyu ramen. Cash only.

osaka_oden_sumiyoshi_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Oden · refined Osaka oden with three broths in the Hotel Nikko basement] A calm, polished oden restaurant two floors below the Hotel Nikko building in Shinsaibashi, open since 2019 and, per one diner, carrying on the style of the late oden house Takokichi. Three different broths are matched to the ingredients. Beyond the classics (tender octopus, thick fried tofu, whale), try the creative pieces: a potato ball wrapped in egg, jaga-butter, wagyu cooked shabu-shabu style in the broth, and the house daikon in white miso with pork belly. Finish with clay-pot rice. Lunch is the bargain: a seasonal tempura set with oden for ¥2,480. Portions are delicate. 10% service charge at dinner. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_menya_tsubaki_teradacho.notes: [Ramen · Taiwan mazesoba made to order in Teradacho] A high-ceilinged, roomy shop five minutes from Teradacho, open since 2017, devoted to Taiwan mazesoba. Buy a ticket, then choose noodle weight (150 or 200 g), spice (mild, medium or spicy) and garlic. The bowl is chewy, wide noodles under spicy minced meat, green onion, egg yolk, fish powder and nori; mix hard, add vinegar halfway to brighten it, then put rice into what's left (¥1,100 with rice). Even the spicy level is manageable, though medium can still make you sweat. A ramen with chashu is on the menu too. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays; Sunday is lunch only.

osaka_akayoroshi_tsuruhashi.notes: [Ramen · light chicken chuka soba by day, obanzai and drinks by night, Tsuruhashi] A small, welcoming spot down a side alley three minutes from Tsuruhashi, open since 2022 and run single-handed on one February visit, cooking ramen and stirring fried rice at once. The Ganso Chuka Soba (¥890) is a surprisingly clear, low-oil soy broth of Tosa Hachikin chicken that clings to thin, smooth noodles; the Akayoroshi soba (¥1,200) goes the other way, heavy on garlic and vegetables, finished with rice like a risotto. Tomato, sesame and horumon ramen round it out. At night it's an izakaya with obanzai lined up on the counter and oden, and the ramen makes a gentle finish. Open until 2:00 on Fridays and Saturdays. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

The Kamisori Drop, a warm-chilled noodle bowl with salt sauce, egg and heaps of green onion, is the sleeper. Add kara-age or a highball set. One diner found the shoyu's noodles too heavy for the soup. Cards and PayPay accepted.

osaka_chuka_soba_ajiemon_tsuruhashi.notes: [Ramen · horse-mackerel chuka soba with Tsuruhashi-market fish, Tsuruhashi] A seven-seat counter on the Tsuruhashi shopping street, open since March 2026 and already well covered, built around aji (horse mackerel) from the local market. The aji fresh-fish shoyu (¥980) is a creamy, rounded bone broth; the aji niboshi shoyu and shio are sharper and leaner, and a limited aji ramen goes rich and cloudy. Noodles are homemade from flour milled in Ikuno, chewy and wheaty, under Kagoshima pork chashu. Order the aji meshi: fresh aji over rice with wasabi, so good it rivals a sushi bar. The menu changes often, and hours have moved to 7:00 openings, so check social media. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients from around Tsuruhashi: aji from a Tsuruhashi market fish shop, flour from Miyake Seifun in Ikuno, vegetables from a local grocer (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles are made from a special blend of flour from Miyake Seifun in the same Ikuno Ward, using a vacuum mixer… resulting in a homemade noodle with a chewy texture and rich wheat flavor." — September 2026, Tsuruhashi 2-chome Black Tsukemen ¥1,250.
"I was amazed by the freshness of the aji itself. Since it's sourced from a local fish market in Tsuruhashi, it's no surprise…" — July 2026, aji don.

osaka_tantanmen_kuro_oni_nishitenma.notes: [Ramen · black-sesame tantanmen in a renovated old house, Nishi-Tenma] A calm, stylish tantanmen shop in a renovated old house down the narrow Oimatsu alley in Nishi-Tenma, easy to mistake for a home, open since 2018. The order is the soupless black-sesame tantanmen: a nearly black, intensely fragrant sesame paste with minced meat over chewy flat noodles, plated like a pasta dish, with spice to your level and rice to finish. The white-sesame tantanmen is the soup version, and a chilled white-sesame bowl appears in summer. Yodare chicken, small gyoza and a drink set make it an evening stop too. One diner found the soup mild. Small sizes available. AMEX and PayPay accepted.

anecdotes.text: "The rich aroma of black sesame fills the air, and the perfect balance of spiciness and sweetness from the sesame creates a delightful bowl. The noodles have just the right thickness and a strong chewiness." — July 2026, soupless black-sesame tantanmen.

"The glossy white sesame soup, vibrant chili oil, and colorful toppings… The depth and nuttiness of the white sesame spread across my palate, followed by the pleasant spiciness of the chili oil and the refreshing numbing sensation of Sichuan peppercorns." — July 2026, limited chilled tantanmen.

osaka_toriya_ume_no_yu_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Yakitori · a Showa-era bathhouse-themed yakitori counter, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A seventeen-seat counter behind a bathhouse-style noren near Shinsaibashi, with Showa pop on the speakers. Ume no Yu once served horse meat, and has returned as a yakitori shop. Start with the omakase set (¥2,800, reserve), four skewers with appetizers and small dishes, or the ¥4,500 course that ends with a mini curry. The grilling is precise: Kyoto Akadori thigh with crisp skin, breast left lightly rare, bone-in wings with rock salt. Order the fried tomato with mascarpone, the mozuku and the potato salad, plus a grilled Tochio aburage. Plenty of shochu. Some skewers sell out, so reserve. Cards accepted.

"The chicken breast was perfectly grilled, lightly salted, and slightly rare inside… the chicken wings had crispy skin, and they were best enjoyed with rock salt!" — November 2025, six-skewer set.

osaka_robata_furoshiki_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Izakaya · charcoal robata open until 5:30 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A stylish third-floor robata izakaya near Nagahoribashi, open since 2023 from 18:00 until 5:30, which draws a late-night Minami crowd. Everything comes off the charcoal or straw fire in front of the counter: whole sanma with grated daikon, a big grilled vegetable platter, butter-soy nagaimo and sirloin cap. The sashimi platter is fresh (one diner waited a while for it), and the mentaiko dashimaki with grilled anago is a standout. Finish with one of several kamameshi or a buttery omurice. Smoking is allowed at the table. Not cheap, but seasonal and carefully made. Closed Wednesdays.

anecdotes.text: "The skin was crispy and the flesh juicy, with a hint of bitterness in some parts. Paired with grated daikon and ponzu sauce, it was a perfect match for drinks." — September 2026, grilled sanma.

osaka_honkaku_robatayaki_hitomukashi_nam.notes: [Izakaya · robata izakaya with a famous seafood lunch bowl, Ura-Namba] A popular robatayaki izakaya in the Ura-Namba back streets, open since 2012, where lunch lines form for seafood bowls. The signature Bakudan don (¥1,800) heaps salmon roe, tuna, negitoro and sea bream over rice; eat it in three stages, first with dashi soy, then with the sesame-dressed sashimi on the side, then with tororo. Seasonal bowls rotate, like a Wakayama shirasu half-raw, half-boiled bowl or a Senshu anago tempura don. Dinner is robata and a sashimi platter served under a cloud of smoke, plus anago nigiri and soft-roe mapo tofu. Weekend breakfast from 7:00. No lunch reservations; arrive early. 5% service charge at dinner.

"When I opened the lid, it was like opening a treasure box, with smoke rising dramatically—such a stylish presentation! Not only was it visually impressive, but the sashimi was also incredibly fresh…" — September 2026, dinner.

osaka_binchotan_yakitori_sasaya_shinsaib.notes: [Yakitori · binchotan chicken on plates until 5 am, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] The main shop of SASAYA, tucked into an alley near Shinsaibashi, grilling morning-fresh chicken over Kishu binchotan and serving it off the skewer on colorful Japanese plates. It's open until 5:00, so it works as a first stop or the last. Try the seseri with green onion, the heart, and the chicken tataki of liver and heart with sesame on a Kutani-style plate; the chicken sashimi and seasonal duck with wasabi are other picks. The counter is friendly and chatty. One diner found it good rather than special. Only two tables, so reserve for groups. ¥418 appetizer charge. Smoking allowed.

osaka_the_9x_osaka_tenma.notes: [Ramen · "French-twist" salmon ramen in a bar-like room, Tenma] A stylish shop near the Okawa river that looks like a bar from outside, open since 2022, from a group with shops in Tokyo and Kyoto. The bowls look like plated pasta. The white salmon ramen floats an espuma over a creamy broth, then piles on smoked salmon, thin chashu, croutons, crisp burdock chips and balsamic, over slightly wavy flat noodles; the salmon tantanmen is the spicy signature. The Genovese mazesoba, rich with basil and cheese, is a good second dish, and the salmon rice set comes alive with broth poured over. One diner found the white salmon broth more salty than salmony. Staff explain the menu patiently. Lunch-led hours; closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.philosophy: "Ramen with a French twist" (shop banner, July 2026 review).

osaka_jinrui_mina_karasa_ga_subete_abeno.notes: [Ramen · graded-spice chige ramen in the Abeno HOOP food hall] A spice-focused counter of the Jinrui Mina Menrui group in the basement food hall of Abeno HOOP, open since 2023. Two bowls carry the name: the 50 (¥1,100), ramen in a flavorful chige soup heavy with chili oil and minced meat on medium-thick noodles, and the soupless 30 (¥1,000). There's also a yukgaejang ramen that one diner likened to Mongolian Tanmen Nakamoto. Spice runs from none through levels 1–4 to Over and the fierce END, which staff suggest only after you've eaten Over; level 2 is already properly hot, and level 1 suits most. The thick chashu soothes the heat, as does a pork rice bowl (¥350). Order, take a buzzer, sit anywhere in the hall.

osaka_mendokoro_fujiyama_jirou_abeno_hoo.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style ramen with a Takaida soy edge in the Abeno HOOP food court] A six-seat partitioned counter in the HOOP basement dining court, open since 2024, serving Jiro-style ramen that leans toward Osaka's Takaida style, with a tangy, stronger soy than usual. Order at the kiosk, pick your garlic, back fat and vegetables, and collect a bowl of extra-thick, chewy noodles under sprouts, cabbage, heaps of green onion and thick chashu. The shio Jiro is powerfully salty; the soupless version is heartier still. Cheddar cheese is the surprise topping that works, and black oolong tea comes free. It's milder than many Jiro shops, which suits newcomers. Under ¥1,000 for a regular. Open until 23:00.

osaka_tsukemen_hirano_tamatsukuri.notes: [Tsukemen · thick whole-wheat tsukemen in kombu water by Tamatsukuri] A tsukemen and mazesoba shop two minutes from Tamatsukuri's north exit, open since 2021; one diner prefers its relaxed pace to the busier JET600 nearby. The noodles are the draw: thick, golden, homemade with whole wheat and served in kombu water, chewy and bouncy, best taken two strands at a time. The house dip is a rich tonkotsu-and-seafood soy with back fat, katsuobushi oil and a whisper of yuzu; spicy (levels 1–3, level 2 is hotter than it sounds) and shio versions too. Finish by diluting the dip with the citrus-scented soup at the counter, or with rice. Tsukemen 200 g is ¥1,000, and large sizes cost a little more. PayPay accepted.
